paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God doesn't hand out righteousness as a paycheck. Paul says the wages of the worker "are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation" (Romans 4:4). But to the one who doesn't work, "but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness" (Romans 4:5). That means you can't earn it, and you don't have to, because you get it by believing God, and that is GOOD news for anybody who has ever tried to out-work their own mistakes.

And Paul makes sure nobody walks away thinking it's only for a certain crowd, because Abraham's faith was credited to him before he was circumcised, so the blessing isn't locked behind a sign or a rule (Romans 4:10). David talks about the same blessing: "Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him" (Romans 4:8). So "the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham's offspring" (Romans 4:16). A promise resting on grace can't be knocked over by your bad week.

So what does faith look like? Abraham looked at his body, about a hundred years old, and still did not waver, "being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised" (Romans 4:21). Faith isn't pretending the problem isn't there, it's trusting that God is bigger than the problem. Paul says those words "it was credited to him" were written for us too, for those who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead (Romans 4:23-24), and Jesus "was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification" (Romans 4:25), so you can rest your whole weight on that, baker.
